corrections.critique: Strongest feature: Dillahunty separates logical exhaustiveness, comparative ranking, and sufficient epistemic warrant, explaining why the highest-ranked hypothesis need not become justified belief when probability assignments remain evidentially underdetermined. Principal limitation: The threshold reference clarifies permissible suspension, but it could distinguish explicitly between belief, credence, and action-guiding choice, since comparative ranking may remain consequential without establishing what historically occurred. Live burden: The pro case must demonstrate not merely that resurrection compares favorably with alternatives, but that its priors and likelihood judgments are reliably grounded and strong enough to overcome rational noncommitment. Locked score: The very strong 94 reflects motion-level relevance, decisive responsiveness, stable qualification, coherent uncertainty calibration, and substantial charity, while modest evidential-warrant and representational limits prevent perfection.
